recYyKPBJ6GIJIBlp.title: Goliath
recYyKPBJ6GIJIBlp.summary: Goliath is a legendary Philistine warrior of giant stature attested to in the Biblical narratives of 1 and 2 Samuel.

recYyeczKVbq0DLzk.title: Jehoiada
recYyeczKVbq0DLzk.summary: Jehoiada in the Hebrew Bible, was a prominent priest in the kingdom of Judah during the reigns of Ahaziah, Athaliah, and Joash. Jehoiada became the brother-in-law of King Ahaziah as a result of his marriage with princess Jehosheba. Both Jehosheba and Ahaziah were children of King Jehoram of Judah. Ahaziah died a year after assuming the throne, which was then usurped by his mother Athaliah, who ordered the execution of all members of the royal family.
recYyeczKVbq0DLzk.desc: Priest in Judah in the Bible

recZ6YiBydClBiVVJ.title: Zebulun
recZ6YiBydClBiVVJ.summary: Zebulun was, according to the Books of Genesis and Numbers, Jacob's tenth son, the last of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite tribe of Zebulun. With Leah as a matriarch, biblical scholars believe the tribe to have been regarded by the text's authors as a part of the original Israelite confederation.
recZ6YiBydClBiVVJ.desc: Biblical figure and son of Jacob and Leah

recZBfXD2bxyCKO6f.title: Zephaniah
recZBfXD2bxyCKO6f.summary: Zephaniah is the name of several people in the Hebrew Bible; the most prominent being the prophet who prophesied in the days of Josiah, king of Judah and is attributed a book bearing his name among the Twelve Minor Prophets. His name is commonly transliterated Sophonias in Bibles translated from the Vulgate or Septuagint. The name might mean "Yahweh has hidden/protected," or "Yah lies in wait". The church father Jerome interpreted the name to mean "the watchman of the Lord".

recZOriotFt9GIf6b.title: Uzziah
recZOriotFt9GIf6b.summary: Uzziah, also known as Azariah, was the tenth king of the ancient Kingdom of Judah, and one of Amaziah's sons. Uzziah was 16 when he became king of Judah and reigned for 52 years. The first 24 years of his reign were as a co-regent with his father, Amaziah.

recZUByYaXzjYwBDp.title: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah
recZUByYaXzjYwBDp.summary: Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah. He succeeded Shebna to become royal steward or prime minister for King Hezekiah of Judah, according to the Hebrew Bible.

recZoEyK9nqfNB6C5.title: Ahira
recZoEyK9nqfNB6C5.summary: Ahira is a Hebrew Bible character. He was a son of Enan and chosen to be chief of the tribe of Naphtali, one of the leaders of the tribes of Israel during The Exodus.

recZsS2Zu0zIDwqdv.title: Samuel
recZsS2Zu0zIDwqdv.summary: Samuel is a figure who, in the narratives of the Hebrew Bible, plays a key role in the transition from the biblical judges to the United Kingdom of Israel under Saul, and again in the monarchy's transition from Saul to David. He is venerated as a prophet in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. In addition to his role in the Jewish Bible/Old Testament, Samuel is mentioned in Jewish rabbinical literature, in the Christian New Testament, and in the second chapter of the Quran. He is also treated in the fifth through seventh books of Antiquities of the Jews, written by the Jewish scholar Josephus in the first century. He is first called "the Seer" in 1 Samuel 9:9.

recZtcxs57c7NXXlg.title: Pekah
recZtcxs57c7NXXlg.summary: Pekah was the eighteenth and penultimate king of Israel. He was a captain in the army of king Pekahiah of Israel, whom he killed to become king. Pekah was the son of Remaliah.

recZzpkHckkrMHT0h.title: Naboth
recZzpkHckkrMHT0h.summary: Naboth was a citizen of Jezreel. According to the Book of Kings in the Hebrew Bible, he was executed by Jezebel, the queen of Israel, so that her husband Ahab could possess his vineyard.
recZzpkHckkrMHT0h.desc: Biblical character in the Book of Kings

reca7COilV04EhZgr.title: List of people named Shemaiah in the Bible
reca7COilV04EhZgr.summary: Shemaiah is the name of several people in the Hebrew Bible :a Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his relatives took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron the eldest son of Obed-edom Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a scribe mentioned as active at the death of David Shemaiah, a prophet in the reign of Rehoboam one of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law Shemaiah, the father of Shimri, listed as a Simeonite five generations before the reign of Hezekiah Shemaiah son of Jeduthun, a Levite in the time of Hezekiah a Levite appointed to "distribute the oblations of the Lord" during the reign of Hezekiah a Levite in the time of Josiah the father of Urijah …

recaK8xpsOSVcWMc2.title: Jabin
recaK8xpsOSVcWMc2.summary: Jabin is a Biblical name meaning 'discerner', or 'the wise'. It may refer to:A king of Hazor at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan, whose overthrow and that of the northern chiefs with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land. The Battle of the Waters of Merom, fought at Lake Hula, was the last of Joshua's battles of which we have any record. Here for the first time the Israelites encountered the iron chariots and horses of the Canaanites. The Israelites killed him and everyone in his city along with all the people in the cities of Madon, Shimron, Achshaph, Debir, and Anab. They then destroyed Hazor by fire.
recaK8xpsOSVcWMc2.desc: Kings of Hazor mentioned in the Hebrew Bible

recauQ3IPfRTuQbBj.title: Noah
recauQ3IPfRTuQbBj.summary: Noah appears as the last of the Antediluvian patriarchs in the traditions of Abrahamic religions. His story appears in the Hebrew Bible, the Quran and Baha'i writings, and extracanonically.
recauQ3IPfRTuQbBj.desc: Biblical prophet known for building an ark

recbHLkz06CSe3C4K.title: Elijah
recbHLkz06CSe3C4K.summary: Elijah was a prophet and miracle worker who lived in the northern kingdom of Israel during the reign of King Ahab, according to the Books of Kings in the Hebrew Bible.

recbO7tUz8fk12ExW.title: Hur (Bible)
recbO7tUz8fk12ExW.summary: Hur was a companion of Moses and Aaron in the Hebrew Bible. He was a member of the Tribe of Judah. His identity remains unclear in the Torah itself, but it is elaborated in rabbinical commentary.
recbO7tUz8fk12ExW.desc: Biblical character; companion of Moses and Aaron (Exod. 17:10–12)

recc4xDKjSwM1pH12.title: Daniel (biblical figure)
recc4xDKjSwM1pH12.summary: Daniel is the main character of the Book of Daniel. According to the Hebrew Bible, Daniel was a noble Jewish youth of Jerusalem taken into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon, serving the king and his successors with loyalty and ability until the time of the Persian conqueror Cyrus, all the while remaining true to the God of Israel. While some conservative scholars hold that Daniel existed and his book was written in the 6th century BCE, most scholars agree that Daniel, as depicted in the Book of Daniel, was not a historical figure, and that the character was probably based on a similar legendary Daniel from earlier traditions.
recc4xDKjSwM1pH12.desc: Protagonist of the Book of Daniel of the Hebrew Bible

image.credit: qgE_ZHxscNNGbA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

reccN1xlFTOq0eIxu.title: Bethuel
reccN1xlFTOq0eIxu.summary: Bethuel, in the Hebrew Bible, was an Aramean man, the youngest son of Nahor and Milcah, the nephew of Abraham, and the father of Laban and Rebecca.

recca9oZ4wL4Gg4SK.title: Meshech
recca9oZ4wL4Gg4SK.summary: In the Bible, Meshech or Mosoch is named as a son of Japheth in Genesis 10:2 and 1 Chronicles 1:5.

reccdFYIq50NyxNej.title: Abraham
reccdFYIq50NyxNej.summary: Abraham is widely revered as a foundational legendary figure among adherents of the eponymous Abrahamic religions. In Judaism, he is the ethnic ancestor and first Hebrew patriarch who began the covenantal relationship between the Jewish people and God; in Christianity, he is regarded as the forebear of Jesus and the spiritual ancestor of all Christians; and in Islam, he is a link in the chain of Islamic prophets that begins with Adam and culminates in Muhammad. Abraham is revered in all other Abrahamic religions, such as the Baháʼí Faith and the Druze faith. He is regarded as the common forefather of both the Arab people through his son Ishmael and the Jewish people through his son Isaac.

recceqSlJUCba6VY5.title: Ammihud
recceqSlJUCba6VY5.summary: Ammihud is the name of several Hebrew Bible figures:The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, the father of Nun, at the time of the Exodus. The father of Shemuel, of the Tribe of Simeon The father of Pedahel, a prince of the Tribe of Naphtali The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai

recclamlHQiKUuV8K.title: Jonadab
recclamlHQiKUuV8K.summary: Jonadab is a figure in the Hebrew Bible, appearing in 2 Samuel 13. He is described in verse 3 as the son of Shimeah, who was the brother of David, making Jonadab a cousin to Amnon as well as his friend. He is called "very wise", usually translated as "very shrewd" (NIV) or "very crafty" (ESV).
recclamlHQiKUuV8K.desc: Character in 2 Samuel; son of Shimeah

reccpdazfRa8RGKt6.title: Abel
reccpdazfRa8RGKt6.summary: Abel is a biblical figure in the Book of Genesis within the Abrahamic religions. Born as the second son of Adam and Eve, the first two humans created by God, he was a shepherd who offered his firstborn flock to God as a religious offering. God accepted Abel's offering but not that of his older brother Cain, leading Cain to kill Abel out of jealousy; some later interpretations suggest that Cain may have slain him with a stone. This act marked the first death in biblical history, making Abel the first murder victim.

recd33WGbx9DkJuTk.title: Nathanael
recd33WGbx9DkJuTk.summary: Nathanael is an English name of Hebrew origin. It is of Biblical origin and holds significance for Jews and Christians. Several figures in both the Old and New Testament bear the name. Figures in the Old Testament, which is transliterated from Hebrew, have their names rendered as Nethanel in English whereas those in the New Testament, which is translated from Greek, have theirs rendered as Nathanael. Since the early 20th century, the most common English spelling is Nathaniel, a change likely influenced by the popularity of other Biblical names ending in -iel. Bearers may use the nicknames Nate or Nathan.

recdAonAgqAfLGdz9.title: Seraiah
recdAonAgqAfLGdz9.summary: Seraiah or Sraya is the name of several people mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, and a name with other non-biblical uses.

recdIZxgxO61iLEXm.title: Levi
recdIZxgxO61iLEXm.summary: Levi was, according to the Book of Genesis, the third of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Levi and the great-grandfather of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Certain religious and political functions were reserved for the Levites.
recdIZxgxO61iLEXm.desc: Biblical figure and son of Jacob and Leah

recdUEBr1HD0OmXeR.title: Caleb
recdUEBr1HD0OmXeR.summary: Caleb is a figure who appears in the Hebrew Bible as a representative of the Tribe of Judah during the Israelites' journey to the Promised Land.

recdZkHDtmoVtSEZh.title: Pashhur
recdZkHDtmoVtSEZh.summary: Pashur or Pashhur was the name of at least two priests contemporary with the prophet Jeremiah and who are mentioned in the Book of Jeremiah. The name is of Egyptian origin, Pš-Ḥr.
recdZkHDtmoVtSEZh.desc: Characters in the Book of Jeremiah

recdZn27T4U42O0LH.title: Hazael
recdZn27T4U42O0LH.summary: Hazael was a king of Aram-Damascus mentioned in the Bible. Under his reign, Aram-Damascus became an empire that ruled over large parts of contemporary Syria and historical Palestine. While he was likely born in the greater Damascus region of today, his place of birth is unknown, with both Bashan and the Beqaa Valley being favoured by different historians.

recdvASnxGfjfmvDM.title: Seth
recdvASnxGfjfmvDM.summary: Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve in the Abrahamic religions. The Hebrew Bible names two of his siblings as Cain and Abel. According to Genesis 4:25, Seth was born after the event of Cain's murder of Abel, and Eve believed that God had appointed him as a replacement for Abel.
recdvASnxGfjfmvDM.desc: Third son of Adam and Eve

rece4MdvDF2ule9OY.title: Korah
rece4MdvDF2ule9OY.summary: Korah, son of Izhar, is an individual who appears in the Biblical Book of Numbers of the Old Testament, known for leading a rebellion against Moses. Some older English translations, as well as the Douay–Rheims Bible, spell the name Core, and many Eastern European translations have "Korak" or "Korey".

receruzYNFLuIW0Kn.title: Amaziah
receruzYNFLuIW0Kn.summary: Amaziah or Amasias may refer to:Amaziah of Judah, the king of Judah A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite Amaziah, a priest of the golden calves at Bethel The father of Joshah, one of the leaders of the tribe of Simeon in the time of Hezekiah

receyzziW4sDhoPTk.title: Jehu (prophet)
receyzziW4sDhoPTk.summary: Jehu son of Hanani was a prophet mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, who was active during the 9th century BC.
receyzziW4sDhoPTk.desc: Biblical prophet and son of Hanani

recfAbfAbrsckOQ2t.title: Joiada
recfAbfAbrsckOQ2t.summary: Joiada is a name found from the form "Jehoiada" in the Hebrew Bible and used alternately in English versions."The Jeshanah Gate was repaired by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They laid its beams and put its doors with their bolts and bars in place"

recfDNqHzhyepDV2z.title: Shechem
recfDNqHzhyepDV2z.summary: Shechem, also spelled Sichem and other variants, was an ancient city in the Southern Levant. Described in ancient Egyptian inscriptions from the 19th century BC as a part of Retjenu, it is also recorded as a Canaanite city in the 14th century BC Amarna letters.
recfDNqHzhyepDV2z.desc: Biblical city in the West Bank

recgfx8iuSsor6yXf.title: Othniel
recgfx8iuSsor6yXf.summary: Othniel was the first of the biblical judges. The etymology of his name is uncertain, but may mean "God/He is my strength" or "God has helped me". In certain texts the name taken in context lends itself to the verbatim translation “The Wrath of God”.

recgkFqZovgbr3pAi.title: Jesus
recgkFqZovgbr3pAi.summary: Jesus, also known as Jesus Christ, Jesus of Nazareth, and by various other names and titles, was a Jewish preacher and religious leader active in the Roman province of Judaea during the 1st century. He is the central figure of Christianity, the world's largest religion. Most branches of Christianity consider Jesus the incarnation of God the Son and the awaited Messiah or Christ. Accounts of Jesus's life are contained in the Gospels, especially the four canonical Gospels of the New Testament.
recgkFqZovgbr3pAi.desc: First-century Jewish preacher and religious leader

recgkzNX07a7kGFYL.title: Paul the Apostle
recgkzNX07a7kGFYL.summary: Paul, commonly known as Paul the Apostle or Saint Paul, was a Christian apostle who spread the teachings of Jesus in the first century AD. For his contributions to the New Testament, he is generally regarded as one of the most important figures of the Apostolic Age, and he also founded several Christian communities in Asia Minor and Europe from the mid-40s to the mid-50s AD.

rechBzMEecm1fl5MJ.title: Er (biblical person)
rechBzMEecm1fl5MJ.summary: In the biblical Book of Genesis, Er was the eldest son of Judah and his Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shuah. He is described as marrying Tamar. According to the text, "the Lord slew" Er because he was wicked, although it does not give any further details. This Er had two brothers, Onan and Shelah.
rechBzMEecm1fl5MJ.desc: Biblical figure; first son of Judah

rechDI5vmWFtiVmYq.title: Jared
rechDI5vmWFtiVmYq.summary: Jared is a given name of Biblical derivation.

rechGwqMPGYsNy5xT.title: Ahaziah
rechGwqMPGYsNy5xT.summary: Ahaziah was the name of two kings mentioned in the Hebrew Bible:Ahaziah of Israel Ahaziah of Judah

rechXwK5tLNyMXgrM.title: Zebah and Zalmunna
rechXwK5tLNyMXgrM.summary: Zebah and Zalmunna were the two kings who led the vast host of the Midianites who invaded the land of Israel, and over whom Gideon gained a great and decisive victory. Zebah and Zalmunna had succeeded in escaping across the Jordan River with a remnant of the Midianite host, but were overtaken at Karkor, probably in the Hauran, and routed by Gideon. The kings were taken alive and brought back across the Jordan; and confessing that they had personally taken part in the killing of Gideon's brothers, they were put to death.
rechXwK5tLNyMXgrM.desc: Kings mentioned in the Hebrew Bible

image.artist: Hieronymus Wierix / After Marten van Cleve

rechda7WMDuW1jBTq.title: Sarah
rechda7WMDuW1jBTq.summary: Sarah is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions. While different Abrahamic faiths portray her differently, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam all depict her character similarly, as that of a pious woman, renowned for her hospitality and beauty, the wife of Abraham, and the mother of Isaac.

rechjMXjFfG41iAfc.title: Caiaphas
rechjMXjFfG41iAfc.summary: Joseph ben Caiaphas was a High Priest of Israel during the first century. In the New Testament, the Gospels of Matthew, Luke and John indicate he was an organizer of the plot to kill Jesus. He is portrayed as presiding over the Sanhedrin trial of Jesus. The primary sources for Caiaphas' life are the New Testament and the writings of the historian Josephus. The latter recorded that Caiaphas was made high priest by the Roman procurator Valerius Gratus after Simon ben Camithus had been deposed.

reci5XsSfPw9RZWBA.title: Joab
reci5XsSfPw9RZWBA.summary: Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was the nephew of King David and the commander of his army according to the Hebrew Bible.
reci5XsSfPw9RZWBA.desc: Nephew of King David of Israel and commander of his army

reciJDq0wUbyVGePr.title: Tychicus
reciJDq0wUbyVGePr.summary: Tychicus was an Asiatic Christian who, with Trophimus, accompanied the Apostle Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem. He is also was with Paul during his imprisonments, either in Caesarea or in Rome, whence the apostle sent him to Ephesus, probably for the purpose of building up and encouraging the church there. In the New Testament, he is mentioned five times.

recil8ETKDbAGI4uh.title: Zadok
recil8ETKDbAGI4uh.summary: Zadok, also spelled Ṣadok, Ṣadoc, Zadoq, Tzadok or Tsadoq, was a Kohen (priest), biblically recorded to be a descendant of Eleazar the son of Aaron. He was the High Priest of Israel during the reigns of David and Solomon as kings of Israel. He aided King David during the revolt of his son Absalom, was subsequently instrumental in bringing Solomon to the throne, and officiated at Solomon's coronation. After Solomon's building of the First Temple in Jerusalem, Zadok was the first High Priest to serve there.

recit3DiamFt2zO0S.title: Isaiah
recit3DiamFt2zO0S.summary: Isaiah was the Israelite prophet, dated to the 8th century BC, after whom the Book of Isaiah is named.

recj26MAojx8FuOsa.title: Enoch
recj26MAojx8FuOsa.summary: Enoch is a biblical figure and patriarch prior to Noah's flood. He is the son of Jared and father of Methuselah.
recj26MAojx8FuOsa.desc: Biblical figure prior to Noah's flood

recjLXb7c8RjZDfMS.title: Zeruiah
recjLXb7c8RjZDfMS.summary: Zeruiah was a sister of King David. According to both the Hebrew Bible and the Babylonian Talmud, Zeruiah was a daughter of Jesse and sister of Abigail, to whom reference is made in 1 Chronicles and 2 Samuel. Zeruiah had three sons, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, David's nephews, all of whom were soldiers in David's army.

recjMT68aIzFLh6cQ.title: Saul
recjMT68aIzFLh6cQ.summary: Saul was a monarch of ancient Israel and Judah and the first king of the United Monarchy according to the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament. His reign, traditionally placed in the late eleventh century BC, marked the transition of the Israelites from a scattered tribal society ruled by various judges to organized statehood.

recjNRR60PAuFtjha.title: Moses
recjNRR60PAuFtjha.summary: In Abrahamic religions, Moses was the Hebrew prophet who led the Israelites out of slavery in the Exodus from Egypt. He is considered the most important prophet in Judaism and Samaritanism, and one of the most important prophets in Christianity, Islam, the Baháʼí Faith, and other Abrahamic religions. According to the Abrahamic scriptures, God dictated the Mosaic Law to Moses, which he wrote down and which formed part of the Torah.

recjOvYXbQXPhGpBN.title: Hoshea
recjOvYXbQXPhGpBN.summary: Hoshea was the nineteenth and last king of the northern Kingdom of Israel and son of Elah. William F. Albright dated his reign to 732–721 BCE, while Edwin R. Thiele offered the dates 732–723 BCE.
recjOvYXbQXPhGpBN.desc: 19th and last King of Northern Israel

recjQ5QgUAAMyIAmE.title: Shebna
recjQ5QgUAAMyIAmE.summary: Shebna was the royal steward in the reign of king Hezekiah of Judah, according to the Hebrew Bible.

recjU9TzJTjllYnUJ.title: Gideon
recjU9TzJTjllYnUJ.summary: Gideon also named Jerubbaal and Jerubbesheth was an Israelite shopeṭ ("judge"), military leader, and prophet whose calling and victory over the Midianites is described in Judges 6–8 in the Hebrew Bible.
recjU9TzJTjllYnUJ.desc: Character in the biblical Book of Judges

recjqxIrJX2UB8DdR.title: Michal
recjqxIrJX2UB8DdR.summary: Michal was, according to the Books of Samuel, a princess of the United Kingdom of Israel. The younger daughter of King Saul, she was the first wife of David, who later became king: first of Judah, then of all Israel, making her queen consort of Israel.

recjwefZcKPa9FN7N.title: Hannah (biblical figure)
recjwefZcKPa9FN7N.summary: Hannah is one of the wives of Elkanah mentioned in the First Book of Samuel. According to the Hebrew Bible, she was the mother of Samuel.
recjwefZcKPa9FN7N.desc: Biblical prophetess, traditional author of the Song of Hannah, mother of Samuel

recjyWBYEzNaB2uZC.title: Athaliah
recjyWBYEzNaB2uZC.summary: Athaliah was the daughter of King Ahab and Queen Jezebel of Israel; she was queen consort of Judah as the wife of King Jehoram, a descendant of King David, and was later queen regnant c. 841–835 BC.

reck3OffwMr5WIKJi.title: Ishmael
reck3OffwMr5WIKJi.summary: In the biblical Book of Genesis, Ishmael was the first son of Abraham. His mother was Hagar, the handmaiden of Abraham's wife Sarah. He died at the age of 137.

reck40BPIsL4eOuMr.title: Omri
reck40BPIsL4eOuMr.summary: Omri was the sixth king of Israel. He was a successful military campaigner who extended the northern kingdom of Israel. Other monarchs from the House of Omri are Ahab, Ahaziah, Joram, and Athaliah. Like his predecessor, king Zimri, who ruled for only seven days, Omri is the second king mentioned in the Bible without a statement of his tribal origin. One possibility, though unproven, is that he was of the tribe of Issachar.

reck4FOoejZddGY7H.title: Ahasuerus
reck4FOoejZddGY7H.summary: Ahasuerus is a name applied in the Hebrew Bible to three rulers of Ancient Persia and to a Babylonian official first appearing in the Tanakh in the Book of Esther and later in the Book of Tobit. It is derived from either "Xerxes" or "Artaxerxes;" both are names of multiple Achaemenid dynasty Persian kings.
reck4FOoejZddGY7H.desc: Name of various rulers in the Hebrew Bible

reckJ4vuXzqDbTrMP.title: Thomas the Apostle
reckJ4vuXzqDbTrMP.summary: Thomas the Apostle also known as Didymus, was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. Thomas is commonly known as "doubting Thomas" because he initially doubted the resurrection of Jesus when he was told of it ; he later confessed his faith on seeing the places where the wounds appeared still fresh on the holy body of Jesus after the Crucifixion of Jesus.

reckVW6qsLQZJbasF.title: Pekah
reckVW6qsLQZJbasF.summary: Pekah was the eighteenth and penultimate king of Israel. He was a captain in the army of king Pekahiah of Israel, whom he killed to become king. Pekah was the son of Remaliah.

reckcSleXhZyNw9hI.title: Abigail
reckcSleXhZyNw9hI.summary: Abigail was an Israelite woman in the Hebrew Bible married to Nabal; she married the future King David after Nabal's death. Abigail was David's third wife, after Ahinoam and Saul's daughter, Michal, whom Saul later married to Palti, son of Laish, when David went into hiding.
reckcSleXhZyNw9hI.desc: Wife of King David in the Bible

recklAsmU2Bd8lfCZ.title: Book of Baruch
recklAsmU2Bd8lfCZ.summary: The Book of Baruch is a deuterocanonical book of the Bible, used in many Christian traditions, such as Catholic and Orthodox churches. In Judaism and Protestant Christianity, it is considered not to be part of the canon, with the Protestant Bibles categorizing it as part of the Biblical apocrypha. The book is named after Baruch ben Neriah, the prophet Jeremiah's scribe who is mentioned at Baruch 1:1, and has been presumed to be the author of the whole work.
recklAsmU2Bd8lfCZ.desc: Deuterocanonical book of the Bible in some Christian traditions

reckpGvSmhqpHrvu6.title: Abishag
reckpGvSmhqpHrvu6.summary: In the Hebrew Bible, Abishag was a beautiful young woman of Shunem chosen to be a helper and servant to King David in his old age. Among Abishag's duties was to lie next to David and pass along her body heat and vigor because "they put covers on him, but he could not get warm".
reckpGvSmhqpHrvu6.desc: Biblical figure, servant to King David

reclPYWgWZWK5ccsg.title: Amoz
reclPYWgWZWK5ccsg.summary: Amoz, also known as Amotz, was the father of the prophet Isaiah, mentioned in Isaiah 1:1; 2:1 and 13:1, and in II Kings 19:2, 20; 20:1. The word "amoz" means strong.

reclqqQjQ1vEw7Rz1.title: Ahikam
reclqqQjQ1vEw7Rz1.summary: Ahikam was one of the five whom, according to the Hebrew Bible, Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah in connection with the discovery of the book of the law.

reclrP11qLpXRCROa.title: Zimri (king)
reclrP11qLpXRCROa.summary: Zimri, was the fifth king of Israel. His reign lasted only seven days. William F. Albright has dated his reign to 876 BCE, while E. R. Thiele offers the date 885 BCE. His story is told in 1 Kings, Chapter 16.

recmAUAIwW85ajksn.title: Naphtali
recmAUAIwW85ajksn.summary: According to the Book of Genesis, Naphtali was the sixth son of Jacob, the second of his two sons born of Bilhah. He was the founder of the Israelite tribe of Naphtali.
recmAUAIwW85ajksn.desc: Biblical figure, son of Jacob and his concubine Bilhah

recmCYRmiSdCy63Fc.title: Reu
recmCYRmiSdCy63Fc.summary: Reu or Ragau, according to Genesis in the Hebrew Bible, was the son of Peleg and the father of Serug, thus being Abraham's great-great-grandfather and the ancestor of the Israelites and Ishmaelites.

recmQCQy94vebCsiC.title: Adoniram
recmQCQy94vebCsiC.summary: Adoniram, the son of Abda, was the tax collector in the United Kingdom of Israel for over forty years, from the late years of King David's reign until the reign of Rehoboam. In the language of the Tanakh, he was "over the tribute", i.e. the levy or forced labor.

recn2SX3r73jFJWhF.title: Nathan (prophet)
recn2SX3r73jFJWhF.summary: Nathan is a prophet in the Hebrew Bible. His actions are described in the Books of Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles.

reco5AjdpK6pP1m0n.title: Enos (biblical figure)
reco5AjdpK6pP1m0n.summary: Enos or Enosh is a figure in the Book of Genesis in the Hebrew Bible. He is described as the first son of Seth who figures in the Generations of Adam, and is also referred to within the genealogies of 1 Chronicles.

reco9eoVJ4n0TOQNx.title: Javan
reco9eoVJ4n0TOQNx.summary: Javan was the fourth son of Noah's son Japheth according to the "Generations of Noah" in the Hebrew Bible. Josephus states the traditional belief that this individual was the ancestor of the Greeks.
reco9eoVJ4n0TOQNx.desc: Son of Japheth and father of the Greeks according to the Bible

recoJAyYl3Qele6ey.title: Balak
recoJAyYl3Qele6ey.summary: Balak was a king of Moab described in the Book of Numbers in the Hebrew Bible, where his dealings with the prophet and Midianite sorcerer Balaam are recounted. Balak tried to engage Balaam for the purpose of cursing the migrating Israelites. The story of Balak is detailed in Numbers 22–24, Judges 11:25, and Micah 6:5. According to Numbers 22:2, and Joshua 24:9, Balak was the son of Zippor.

recoklD2cyUxjCR8C.title: Shedeur
recoklD2cyUxjCR8C.summary: Shedeur is a given name. Notable people with the name include:Shedeur Sanders, American football player Shedeur, a minor figure in the Hebrew Bible

recon2L7e7FUrd0zD.title: Achish
recon2L7e7FUrd0zD.summary: Achish is a name used in the Hebrew Bible for two Philistine rulers of Gath. It is perhaps only a general title of royalty, applicable to the Philistine kings. The two kings of Gath, which most scholars identify as Tell es-Safi, are:The monarch, described as "Achish the king of Gath", with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul. He is called Abimelech, meaning "father of the king", in the superscription of Psalm 34. It was probably this same king, or his son with the same name, described as "Achish, the son of Maoch", to whom David reappeared a second time at the head of a band of 600 warriors.

recorTh9mzZLSgrB5.title: Anak
recorTh9mzZLSgrB5.summary: Anak is a figure in the Hebrew Bible. His descendants are mentioned in narratives concerning the conquest of Canaan by the Israelites. According to the Book of Numbers, Anak was a forefather of the Anakim, a Rephaite tribe according to Deuteronomy 2:11. In their report, ten of the twelve Israelite spies associated the Anakim with the Nephilim of Genesis 6:1–4.

recoxUPwUPGU1IP9X.title: Apollos
recoxUPwUPGU1IP9X.summary: Apollos was a 1st-century Alexandrian Jewish Christian mentioned several times in the New Testament. A contemporary and colleague of Paul the Apostle, he played an important role in the early development of the churches of Ephesus and Corinth.

recp3sTywycVRJFZt.title: Amalek
recp3sTywycVRJFZt.summary: Amalek was a nation described in the Hebrew Bible as a staunch enemy of the Israelites. The name "Amalek" can refer to the nation's founder, a grandson of Esau; his descendants, the Amalekites; or the territories of Amalek, which they inhabited.

recpPNbR5X8rHlhYQ.title: Eliab
recpPNbR5X8rHlhYQ.summary: Eliab, also spelled Eliaab, is a male name, held by three people in the Hebrew Bible, respectively the sons of Helon, Pallu, and, most significantly, Jesse.

recpvMKljbEMuiK9e.title: Andrew the Apostle
recpvMKljbEMuiK9e.summary: Andrew the Apostle was an apostle of Jesus. According to the New Testament, he was a fisherman and one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus.

recpvQCt0PY7dySM7.title: Aholibamah
recpvQCt0PY7dySM7.summary: Aholibamah is an eight-time referenced matriarch in the biblical record.

recpvlXkEN7EVeDZn.title: Abiathar
recpvlXkEN7EVeDZn.summary: Abiathar, in the Hebrew Bible, is a son of Ahimelech or Ahijah, High Priest at Nob, the fourth in descent from Eli and the last of Eli's House to be a High Priest.

recqDQWQP9P7218TS.title: Uriah (prophet)
recqDQWQP9P7218TS.summary: Uriah is a prophet and martyr mentioned in the Book of Jeremiah.

recqIoG1fkaNWJ1y0.title: Isaac
recqIoG1fkaNWJ1y0.summary: Isaac is the second Hebrew patriarch in Judaism and an important figure in the Abrahamic religions, including Samaritanism, Christianity, Islam, the Baháʼí Faith, and Rastafari. Isaac first appears in the Torah, in which he is the son of Abraham and Sarah, the father of Jacob and Esau, and the grandfather of the twelve tribes of Israel.
recqIoG1fkaNWJ1y0.desc: Biblical patriarch, son of Abraham and Sarah

recqQthL4TAHb0KeC.title: Rehoboam
recqQthL4TAHb0KeC.summary: Rehoboam was, according to the Hebrew Bible, the last monarch of the United Kingdom of Israel, though his reign over the unified state was brief; after the Northern and Southern kingdoms were divided, he became the first king of the Kingdom of Judah. He was a son of and the successor to Solomon and a grandson of David.
recqQthL4TAHb0KeC.desc: Biblical figure; first monarch of the Kingdom of Judah

recqXcKzSpUe7lXej.title: Cushi
recqXcKzSpUe7lXej.summary: The word Cushi or Kushi is a term used in the Hebrew Bible to refer to a dark-skinned person of African descent, equivalent to Greek Αἰθίοψ "Aithíops". However, today the term is generally understood to be a racial slur for people of African descent.
recqXcKzSpUe7lXej.desc: Hebrew Bible term for dark-skinned African

recqejs2MEv6iwkuw.title: Nicodemus
recqejs2MEv6iwkuw.summary: Nicodemus is a New Testament figure venerated as a saint in a number of Christian traditions. He is depicted as a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin who is drawn to hear Jesus's teachings. Like Lazarus, Nicodemus is not mentioned in the synoptic Gospels, but only by John, who devotes more than half of Chapter 3 of his gospel and a few verses of Chapter 7 to Nicodemus; and, lastly, mentions him in Chapter 19.
recqejs2MEv6iwkuw.desc: Pharisee, biblical figure appearing in the Gospel of John

recqnmaHGY0H06enn.title: Agag
recqnmaHGY0H06enn.summary: Agag is a Northwest Semitic name or title applied to a biblical king. It has been suggested that "Agag" was a dynastic name of the kings of Amalek, just as Pharaoh was used as a dynastic name for the ancient Egyptians. The etymology is uncertain, according to John L. McKenzie (1995), while Cox (1884) suggested "High."
recqnmaHGY0H06enn.desc: Northwest Semitic name or title applied to a biblical king

recr8Qrl4yVCFfjvU.title: Eliab
recr8Qrl4yVCFfjvU.summary: Eliab, also spelled Eliaab, is a male name, held by three people in the Hebrew Bible, respectively the sons of Helon, Pallu, and, most significantly, Jesse.

recrRAVkDKZCXTSl7.title: Phinehas
recrRAVkDKZCXTSl7.summary: According to the Hebrew Bible, Phinehas was a priest during the Exodus. The grandson of Aaron and son of Eleazar, the High Priests, he distinguished himself as a youth at Shittim with his zeal against the heresy of Peor.
recrRAVkDKZCXTSl7.desc: Biblical priest and prophet who opposed the heresy of Peor

recrbd7DEzjHDamsf.title: Kehath
recrbd7DEzjHDamsf.summary: According to the Torah, Kehath or Kohath was the second of the sons of Levi and the patriarchal founder of the Kehathites, one of the four main divisions of the Levites in biblical times. In some apocryphal texts, such as the Testament of Levi and the Book of Jubilees, Levi's wife, Kehath's mother, is Milkah, a daughter of Aram.

recrmgFbC93CpVLsa.title: Shimei
recrmgFbC93CpVLsa.summary: Shimei is the name of a number of persons referenced in the Hebrew Bible and Rabbinical literature.The second son of Gershon and grandson of Levi. The family of the Shimeites, as a branch of the tribe of Levi, is mentioned in Numbers 3:18, 21; 1 Chronicles 23:7, 10, 11 ; and in Zechariah 12:13. In the New Testament the name occurs in Luke 3:26, spelled Semei in the King James Version.

recsU2ZSdzBvDqzgI.title: Jacob
recsU2ZSdzBvDqzgI.summary: Jacob, later given the name Israel, is the third Hebrew patriarch in Judaism and an important figure in the Abrahamic religions. He first appears in the Torah, where he is described in the Book of Genesis as a son of Isaac and Rebecca. Accordingly, alongside his older fraternal twin brother Esau, Jacob's paternal grandparents are Abraham and Sarah and his maternal grandfather is Bethuel, whose wife is not mentioned. He is said to have bought Esau's birthright and, with his mother's help, deceived his aging father to bless him instead of Esau.

recsgTN9HO1wPR5qb.title: Micaiah
recsgTN9HO1wPR5qb.summary: Micaiah, son of Imlah, is a prophet in the Hebrew Bible. He is one of the four disciples of Elijah.

recsyU2HqpyE9PeTo.title: Jehoram
recsyU2HqpyE9PeTo.summary: Jehoram was the name of several individuals in the Tanakh. The female version of this name is Athaliah.The son of Toi, King of Hamath who was sent by his father to congratulate David on the occasion of his victory over Hadadezer Jehoram of Israel or Joram, King of Israel Jehoram of Judah or Joram, King of Judah A Levite of the family of Gershom A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in Judah

rect0HgZKMJNmCSiU.title: Amos (prophet)
rect0HgZKMJNmCSiU.summary: Amos was one of the Twelve Minor Prophets of the Hebrew Bible and Christian Old Testament. According to the Bible, Amos was the older contemporary of Hosea and Isaiah and was active c. 760–755 BC during the rule of kings Jeroboam II of Israel and Uzziah of the Kingdom of Judah and is portrayed as being from the southern Kingdom of Judah yet preaching in the northern Kingdom of Israel (Samaria). The prophet is characterized as speaking against an increased disparity between the wealthy and the poor with themes of justice, God's omnipotence, and divine judgment. The Book of Amos is attributed to him.

rectAKOMFVWfGYUGW.title: Nun (biblical figure)
rectAKOMFVWfGYUGW.summary: Nun, in the Hebrew Bible, was a man from the Tribe of Ephraim, grandson of Ammihud, son of Elishama, and father of Joshua.

rectCt5FFUjDdSPnY.title: Bildad
rectCt5FFUjDdSPnY.summary: Bildad, the Shuhite, was one of Job's three friends who visited the patriarch in the Hebrew Bible's Book of Job. He was a descendant of Shuah, son of Abraham and Keturah, whose family lived in the deserts of Arabia, or a resident of the district. In speaking with Job, his intent was consolation, but he became an accuser, asking Job what he has done to deserve God's wrath.
rectCt5FFUjDdSPnY.desc: Biblical figure, an associate of Job

rectDn5oa2vLcaeVF.title: Obed (biblical figure)
rectDn5oa2vLcaeVF.summary: Obed, in the Bible, was a son of Boaz and Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse, the grandfather of Israel’s King David.
rectDn5oa2vLcaeVF.desc: Son of Boaz and Ruth in the Hebrew Bible

rectGDQCkKqZ6LgGB.title: Asher
rectGDQCkKqZ6LgGB.summary: Asher, in the Book of Genesis, was the younger of the two sons of Jacob and Zilpah, who was the handmaid of Jacob's wife Leah, and Jacob's eighth son overall. He was the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Asher.
rectGDQCkKqZ6LgGB.desc: Biblical figure and son of Jacob and Zilpah

rectKmSGswWg5Hx4b.title: Joses
rectKmSGswWg5Hx4b.summary: Joses is a name, usually regarded as a form of Joseph, occurring many times in the New Testament:Joses, one of the four "brothers" of Jesus Joses or Joseph, son of a Mary of Clopas and brother of a James, mentioned in Mark 15:40, Mark 15:47, and Matthew 27:56 Joses or Joseph, the real name of Barnabas according to Acts 4:36 There is also a Ἰησοῦ or a Ἰωσή in Luke 3:29

recthlE4FTgDZvDef.title: Dinah
recthlE4FTgDZvDef.summary: In the Hebrew Bible’s Book of Genesis, Dinah was the seventh child and only named daughter of Leah and the Israelite patriarch, Jacob. An account of her rape by Shechem, son of a Canaanite or Hivite prince, and the subsequent revenge taken by Dinah's brothers Simeon and Levi, commonly referred to as the rape of Dinah, is told in Genesis 34.
recthlE4FTgDZvDef.desc: Daughter of Jacob in Hebrew Bible

rectkXUkoQk15fBk0.title: Saint Titus
rectkXUkoQk15fBk0.summary: Titus was an early Christian missionary and church leader, a companion and disciple of Paul the Apostle, mentioned in several of the Pauline epistles including the Epistle to Titus. He is believed to be a Gentile converted to Christianity by Paul and, according to tradition, he was consecrated as Bishop of the Island of Crete.

recto9z3tEOnLjVOi.title: Reuben (son of Jacob)
recto9z3tEOnLjVOi.summary: Reuben or Reuven was the first of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, according to the Book of Genesis. He was a disappointment to Jacob and lost the pre-eminent position which should have been his as Jacob's firstborn. He was the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Reuben.
recto9z3tEOnLjVOi.desc: Biblical figure and son of Jacob and Leah

rectvs8PWInJwhM9K.title: Zebedee
rectvs8PWInJwhM9K.summary: Zebedee, according to the synoptic gospels, was the father of James and John, two apostles of Jesus. The gospels also suggest that he was the husband of Salome; whereas Mark 15:40 names the women present at the crucifixion as "Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and of Joses, and Salome," the parallel passage in Matthew 27:56 has "Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's children." The Catholic Encyclopedia concludes that the Salome of Mark 15:40 is probably identical with the mother of the sons of Zebedee in Matthew.
rectvs8PWInJwhM9K.desc: Father of James and John, two disciples of Jesus

recu1NkHTdTZhdbo7.title: Milcah
recu1NkHTdTZhdbo7.summary: Milcah was the daughter of Haran and the wife of Nahor, according to the genealogies of Genesis. She is identified as the mother of Bethuel and grandmother of Rebecca and Laban in biblical tradition, and some texts of the Midrash have identified her as Sarah's sister.

recu8J5n677Bmu6qP.title: Cush (Bible)
recu8J5n677Bmu6qP.summary: Cush or Kush, according to the Hebrew Bible, was the oldest son of Ham and a grandson of Noah. He was the brother of Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan. Cush was the father of Nimrod and Havilah.

recuAalSpGhVahIhx.title: Midian
recuAalSpGhVahIhx.summary: Midian was a geographical region in the Tabuk Province of modern-day Saudi Arabia, mentioned in the Hebrew Bible and Quran. William G. Dever states that biblical Midian was in the "northwest Arabian Peninsula, on the east shore of the Gulf of Aqaba on the Red Sea", an area which contained at least 14 inhabited sites during the Late Bronze and early Iron Ages. The Hebrew Bible refers to Midian, a son of Abraham and his wife Keturah, and lists his immediate descendants, the "Midianites".
recuAalSpGhVahIhx.desc: Place mentioned in the Hebrew Bible and Quran

recuAr93KELnhw1t2.title: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
recuAr93KELnhw1t2.summary: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are figures from chapter 3 of the biblical Book of Daniel. In the narrative, the three Jewish men are thrown into a fiery furnace by Nebuchadnezzar II, King of Babylon for refusing to bow to the king's image. The three are preserved from harm, and the king sees four men walking in the flames, "the fourth ... like a son of God". They are first mentioned in Daniel 1, where alongside Daniel they are brought to Babylon to study Chaldean Aramaic language and literature with a view to serving at the King's court, and their Hebrew names are replaced with Babylonian names.
recuAr93KELnhw1t2.desc: Characters in the Book of Daniel

recucD2O1lew9zZg3.title: Zebah and Zalmunna
recucD2O1lew9zZg3.summary: Zebah and Zalmunna were the two kings who led the vast host of the Midianites who invaded the land of Israel, and over whom Gideon gained a great and decisive victory. Zebah and Zalmunna had succeeded in escaping across the Jordan River with a remnant of the Midianite host, but were overtaken at Karkor, probably in the Hauran, and routed by Gideon. The kings were taken alive and brought back across the Jordan; and confessing that they had personally taken part in the killing of Gideon's brothers, they were put to death.
recucD2O1lew9zZg3.desc: Kings mentioned in the Hebrew Bible

image.artist: Hieronymus Wierix / After Marten van Cleve

recudNaaadFm2BdYm.title: Haggai
recudNaaadFm2BdYm.summary: Haggai or Aggeus was a Hebrew prophet active during the building of the Second Temple in Jerusalem, one of the twelve minor prophets in the Hebrew Bible, and the author or subject of the Book of Haggai. He is known for his prophecy in 520 BC, commanding the Jews to rebuild the Temple. He was the first of three post-exilic prophets from the Neo-Babylonian Exile of the House of Judah, who belonged to the period of Jewish history which began after the return from captivity in Babylon. His name means "my holidays".

recukYvuhVi3jljKz.title: Queen of Sheba
recukYvuhVi3jljKz.summary: The Queen of Sheba, named Bilqis in Arabic and Makeda in Geʽez, is a figure first mentioned in the Hebrew Bible. In the original story, she brings a caravan of valuable gifts for Solomon, the fourth King of Israel and Judah. This account has undergone extensive elaborations in Judaism, Ethiopian Christianity, and Islam. It has consequently become the subject of one of the most widespread and fertile cycles of legends in West Asia and Northeast Africa, as well as in other regions where the Abrahamic religions have had a significant impact.
recukYvuhVi3jljKz.desc: Historical figure in the Abrahamic religions

recv0dAY2ULzJ687g.title: Aaron
recv0dAY2ULzJ687g.summary: According to the Hebrew Bible, Aaron was an Israelite prophet, high priest, and the elder brother of Moses. Information about Aaron comes exclusively from religious texts, such as the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament, and the Quran.

recvAB7vkczUEFH8Z.title: John the Apostle
recvAB7vkczUEFH8Z.summary: John the Apostle, also known as Saint John the Beloved and, in Eastern Orthodox Christianity, Saint John the Theologian, was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. Generally listed as the youngest apostle, he was the son of Zebedee and Salome. His brother James was another of the Twelve Apostles. The Church Fathers identify him as John the Evangelist, John of Patmos, John the Elder, and the Beloved Disciple, and then claimed that he outlived the remaining apostles and was the only one to die of natural causes, although modern scholars are divided on the veracity of these claims.

recvERj933nJGf61T.title: Gedaliah
recvERj933nJGf61T.summary: Gedaliah was a person from the Bible who was a governor of Yehud province. He was also the son of Ahikam, who saved the prophet Jeremiah.

recvV3hxT3VINGuwx.title: Ishmael
recvV3hxT3VINGuwx.summary: In the biblical Book of Genesis, Ishmael was the first son of Abraham. His mother was Hagar, the handmaiden of Abraham's wife Sarah. He died at the age of 137.

recvZksoA0NmFrYZ7.title: Miriam
recvZksoA0NmFrYZ7.summary: Miriam is described in the Hebrew Bible as the daughter of Amram and Jochebed, and the older sister of Moses and Aaron. She was a prophetess and first appears in the Book of Exodus.

recwPUzr2MyOjkyLd.title: Ahitophel
recwPUzr2MyOjkyLd.summary: Ahitophel, Achitofel, or Ahithophel, according to the Hebrew Bible, was a counselor of King David and a man greatly renowned for his wisdom. During Absalom's attempt to usurp the throne, he deserted David and supported Absalom, whom he then turned to as an advisor. To counteract Ahitophel's counsel, the fleeing David sent his friend Hushai back to Absalom. Seeing that his advice against David had not been followed due to Hushai's influence, Ahithophel surmised that the revolt would fail, returned to his hometown of Giloh, and hanged himself. He was buried in "the sepulcher of his fathers".

recwcML6FMulTblKH.title: Samson
recwcML6FMulTblKH.summary: Samson was the last of the judges of the ancient Israelites mentioned in the Book of Judges and one of the last leaders who "judged" the twelve tribes of Israel before the institution of the monarchy. He is sometimes regarded as an Israelite version of the popular Near Eastern folk hero archetype also embodied by the Sumerian Gilgamesh and Enkidu, as well as the Greek Heracles. Samson was given superhuman powers by God in the form of extreme strength.
recwcML6FMulTblKH.desc: Important character from the Book of Judges of the Hebrew Bible

recwqt4vhH8t9M6lf.title: Pharaohs in the Bible
recwqt4vhH8t9M6lf.summary: The Bible makes reference to various pharaohs of Egypt. These include unnamed pharaohs in events described in the Torah, as well as several later named pharaohs, some of whom were historical or can be identified with historical pharaohs.

recwqzXQjpmdyyW9y.title: Dan (son of Jacob)
recwqzXQjpmdyyW9y.summary: According to the Book of Genesis, Dan was Jacob's fifth son and the first of the two sons of Jacob and Bilhah. His mother, Bilhah, was Rachel's handmaid, who became one of Jacob's concubines. In the biblical narrative, he is the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Dan. He was the father of Hushim, according to Genesis 46:23, and Samson was a descendant of Dan.
recwqzXQjpmdyyW9y.desc: Biblical figure and the fifth son of Jacob through his concubine Bilhah

recwrDYUkCdyU3t85.title: Asaph (biblical figure)
recwrDYUkCdyU3t85.summary: Asaph is the name of three men from the Hebrew Bible.Asaph, the father of Joah The articles related to the son of Berachiah and descendant of Kohath refer to the same person: Asaph, son of Berachiah the Gershonite. Together with Heman, the grandson of the Israelite prophet Samuel, he and his male descendants were set aside by King David to worship God in song and music. He authored Psalm 50, and Psalms 73 to 83. Asaph, a Levite descendant of Kohath Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest under the Persian king Artaxerxes I Longimanus
recwrDYUkCdyU3t85.desc: Multiple men from the Hebrew Bible

recx0o0Q5Ekmf6zFv.title: Gershon
recx0o0Q5Ekmf6zFv.summary: According to the Torah, Gershon was the eldest of the sons of Levi, and the patriarchal founder of the Gershonites, one of the four main divisions among the Levites in biblical times. The Gershonites were charged with the care of the outer tabernacle including components such as the tent and its covering, screens, doors, and hangings. Biblical scholars regard the name as being essentially the same as "Gershom", which appears to mean "a sojourner there", and it is Gershom rather than Gershon who is sometimes listed in the Book of Chronicles as a founder of one of the principal Levite factions. The Torah names Gershon's sons as Libni and Shimei.

recx7usC4ShQ2PH7M.title: Hebron (biblical figure)
recx7usC4ShQ2PH7M.summary: According to the Torah, Hebron was a son of Kohath and grandson of Levi, consequently being the brother of Amram and uncle of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses. Hebron is portrayed in the text as the founder of the Hebronite clan of Levites; however, on some occasions, the Book of Chronicles treats the Hebronites as being distinct from the descendants of Kohath.
recx7usC4ShQ2PH7M.desc: Patriarch: son of Kohath and grandson of Levi

recxCpuPqJTTZalKd.title: Gilead
recxCpuPqJTTZalKd.summary: Gilead or Gilad is the ancient, historic, biblical name of the mountainous northern part of the region of Transjordan, present-day Jordan. The region is bounded in the west by the Jordan River, in the north by the deep ravine of the river Yarmouk and the region of Bashan, and in the southwest by what were known during antiquity as the "plains of Moab", with no definite boundary to the east. In some cases, "Gilead" is used in the Bible to refer to all the region east of the Jordan River. Gilead is situated in modern-day Jordan, corresponding roughly to the Irbid, Ajloun, Jerash and Balqa Governorates.
recxCpuPqJTTZalKd.desc: Northern part of the region of Transjordan, also the name of several biblical figures

recxH9O2y9AMy6TDM.title: Shelah (son of Judah)
recxH9O2y9AMy6TDM.summary: According to the Bible, Shelah/Shela was the third son of Judah, and was born at Chezib, which can be identified with an unknown town in the vicinity of Mareshah.
recxH9O2y9AMy6TDM.desc: Biblical figure; third son of Judah

recxJQqsngI2rJbuw.title: Jael
recxJQqsngI2rJbuw.summary: Jael or Yael is a heroine of the Bible who aids the Israelites in their war with King Jabin of the city of Hazor in Canaan by killing Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army. This episode is depicted in chapters 4 and 5 of the Book of Judges. According to that account, after Sisera's defeat by the Israelite leader Barak in the Battle of Mount Tabor, he seeks refuge in the tent of Jael, who kills him by driving a tent peg through his skull near the great tree in Zaanaim near Kedesh.

recxj2mVzk0u300vz.title: Menahem
recxj2mVzk0u300vz.summary: Menahem or Menachem was the sixteenth king of the northern Israelite Kingdom of Israel. He was the son of Gadi, and the founder of the dynasty known as the House of Gadi or House of Menahem.

recxkR6HLJD0xWE6R.title: Jeroboam
recxkR6HLJD0xWE6R.summary: Jeroboam I, frequently cited Jeroboam son of Nebat, was the first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel following a revolt of the ten tribes against Rehoboam that put an end to the United Monarchy. According to the book of 1 Kings, he reigned for 22 years and "there was war continually between Rehoboam and Jeroboam". Jeroboam also fought Abijam son of Rehoboam king of Judah. Jeroboam is often described as "doing evil in the sight of the Lord".

recxxH0xyhQyXuyh2.title: Jethro (biblical figure)
recxxH0xyhQyXuyh2.summary: In the Hebrew Bible, Jethro was Moses's father-in-law, a Kenite shepherd and priest of Midian, sometimes called Reuel. In Exodus, Moses's father-in-law is initially referred to as "Reuel" but afterwards as "Jethro". He was also identified as the father of Hobab in Numbers 10:29, though Judges 4:11 identifies him as Hobab.

recy4HxEvjwgHmL9G.title: Heman the Ezrahite
recy4HxEvjwgHmL9G.summary: Heman the Ezrahite is the author of Psalm 88 in the Hebrew Bible, according to the Psalm's colophon.
recy4HxEvjwgHmL9G.desc: Author of part of the Hebrew Bible

recyDlo13a3T5DDGh.title: Eleazar
recyDlo13a3T5DDGh.summary: Eleazar or Elazar was a priest in the Hebrew Bible, the second High Priest, succeeding his father Aaron after he died. He was a nephew of Moses.
recyDlo13a3T5DDGh.desc: High Priest of Israel and son of Aaron

recyGoqLyubply8DF.title: Pharaohs in the Bible
recyGoqLyubply8DF.summary: The Bible makes reference to various pharaohs of Egypt. These include unnamed pharaohs in events described in the Torah, as well as several later named pharaohs, some of whom were historical or can be identified with historical pharaohs.

recyNusCmwtrDBSab.title: Jehoshaphat
recyNusCmwtrDBSab.summary: Jehoshaphat, according to the Hebrew Bible, was the son of Asa, and the fourth king of the Kingdom of Judah, in succession to his father. His children included Jehoram, who succeeded him as king. His mother was Azubah. Historically, his name has sometimes been connected with the Valley of Josaphat.
recyNusCmwtrDBSab.desc: Fourth king of the Kingdom of Judah

recyOsE7tW60nOWh3.title: Ehud
recyOsE7tW60nOWh3.summary: Ehud ben‑Gera is described in the biblical Book of Judges chapter 3 as a judge who was sent by God to deliver the Israelites from Moabite domination. He is described as being left-handed and a member of the Tribe of Benjamin.
recyOsE7tW60nOWh3.desc: Israelite described in the biblical Book of Judges

recyWfFMHv6ZLJkxq.title: Sihon
recyWfFMHv6ZLJkxq.summary: Sihon was an Amorite king mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, king of Ashtaroth, who refused to let the Israelites pass through his country. Chronicled in Numbers, he was defeated by Moses and the Israelites at the battle of Jahaz. He and Og were said to be the two kings Moses defeated on the east side of the Jordan river.
recyWfFMHv6ZLJkxq.desc: Amorite king mentioned in the Hebrew Bible

recya4tTkl2NXT35H.title: Japheth
recya4tTkl2NXT35H.summary: Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah in the Book of Genesis. In the narrative of the Hebrew Bible, he plays a role in the story of Noah's drunkenness and the curse of Ham, and subsequently in the Table of Nations, he is named as the ancestor of the peoples of the Aegean Sea, Anatolia, Caucasus, Greece, and elsewhere in Eurasia. In medieval and early modern European tradition, he was considered to be the progenitor of the European peoples.

recyuyvniLPCMOZyl.title: Cainan
recyuyvniLPCMOZyl.summary: Cainan is mentioned in the Septuagint, the Greek translation of the Book of Genesis, the Book of Jubilees and the genealogy of Jesus given in Luke 3:36 in the New Testament. He is described as a son of Arpachshad and father of Salah, who lived in the time between Noah and Abraham.
recyuyvniLPCMOZyl.desc: Biblical figure omitted from the Masoretic genealogies

reczabgSpj7QAzpHQ.title: Sennacherib
reczabgSpj7QAzpHQ.summary: Sennacherib was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 705 BC until his assassination in 681 BC. The second king of the Sargonid dynasty, Sennacherib is one of the most famous Assyrian kings for the role he plays in the Hebrew Bible, which describes his campaign in the Levant. Other events of his reign include his destruction of the city of Babylon in 689 BC and his renovation and expansion of the last great Assyrian capital, Nineveh.
reczabgSpj7QAzpHQ.desc: King of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, 705–681 BC

reczuS92gSUORr83E.title: Pontius Pilate
reczuS92gSUORr83E.summary: Pontius Pilate was the fifth governor of the Roman province of Judaea, serving under Emperor Tiberius from 26/27 to 36/37 AD. He is best known for being the official who presided over the trial of Jesus and ultimately ordered his crucifixion. Pilate's importance in Christianity is underscored by his prominent place in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. Because the gospels portray Pilate as reluctant to execute Jesus, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church believes that Pilate became a Christian and venerates him as both a martyr and a saint.
reczuS92gSUORr83E.desc: Roman governor of Judea and condemner of Jesus
